body:
## What to build

Make ordinary dplyr column selection and renaming work on a materialized SQLite Margin result with Margin order. Direct materialization must preserve its documented order without returning lazy metadata that breaks subsequent public operations.

This does not add an ordering guarantee to tables derived through later dplyr verbs.

## Reproduction and observed behavior

Confirmed on unmodified [6a5f611](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/commit/6a5f611d41bd462f3c933edea1dd0b9861d6e892), installed in an isolated library and exercised from fresh R processes without testthat. R 4.6.1, dplyr 1.2.1, dbplyr 2.6.0, DBI 1.3.0, RSQLite 3.53.3.

1. Copy a two-row tibble into an in-memory SQLite database: character `g = c("a", "b")`, integer `v = 1:2`.
2. Call `summarize_with_margins()` with `total = sum(v, na.rm = TRUE)`, `.grouping = rollup(g)`, `.margin_label = NULL`, and `.sort = "last"`.
3. Materialize it with `m <- compute(query)`. Directly collecting `m` succeeds and returns the correct three rows.
4. Apply `select(m, g)`.

Expected: a valid lazy projection which can be collected to obtain the three public grouping values. No order is required after this projection.

Actual: query construction fails with `purrr::map_chr(): In index: 1. Result must be length 1, not 0.` Renaming a public measure column also fails.

An independent three-row fixture confirms both failures. Filter, mutate, and arrange still work. An ordinary grouped summary followed by arrange, compute, and select succeeds. A pre-materialization select is also a different, working path.

## Contract, diagnosis, and history

[ADR 0031](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/6a5f611d41bd462f3c933edea1dd0b9861d6e892/design/adr/0031-preserve-sqlite-typed-dimensions-under-margin-order.md) retains ordinary dbplyr behavior after the result. [ADR 0018](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/6a5f611d41bd462f3c933edea1dd0b9861d6e892/design/adr/0018-order-margin-results-by-grouping-structure.md) limits the ordering promise; it does not make ordinary column selection unsupported.

[The dedicated compute method](https://github.com/sayuks/marginplyr/blob/6a5f611d41bd462f3c933edea1dd0b9861d6e892/R/sqlite-typed-order.R) returns an arranged table with a raw SQL rowid expression. On a later projection, dbplyr's `rename_order()` expects an expression with a column name, but the raw SQL expression supplies a zero-length name and violates an internal invariant.

An ordinary table explicitly arranged by `sql("rowid")` reproduces the upstream limitation. Here the caller did not write that expression: marginplyr introduced it while implementing its public materialization contract. Keep that distinction; the ticket concerns the generated result's compatibility, not a request to repair every raw-SQL order expression in dbplyr.

The same dependencies and fixture succeed on pre-#640 code (`ad851dbefe99cf1cf6987dc5f0716f6a13d3873b`) and fail before #653 (`d4ea5f09d5698a6a89b68ecfd62ad450a4089bba`) and at the investigated head. This is a #640 / #650 regression. Existing tests check compute followed directly by collect, or select before compute; those do not exercise compute followed by select.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] After direct materialization of first/last SQLite Margin order, selecting or renaming public columns succeeds and produces the expected values and row count.
- [ ] Preserve Margin order for direct collection of the materialized result, declared types, and the public-only physical table schema. Internal order columns must not leak.
- [ ] Keep ordinary downstream filter/mutate/arrange working. Do not require later projections or renames to preserve the original Margin order.
- [ ] Preserve existing handling of rowid-alias collisions and all supported unsorted/ordinary backend paths.
- [ ] Add regressions that explicitly execute compute before select/rename, with ordinary dbplyr controls and independent expected values, and run the required package checks.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately). Other materialization fixes may overlap in code, but their behavior is not a prerequisite.

title: Allow column selection and renaming after materializing SQLite Margin order
